segments.title: Chương 66: 0066 [Cô Biên Quan Nguyệt, trường chúng tôi rất coi trọng con trai cô]
segments.content:
Rongcheng Train Station.

"Goodbye!"

"Goodbye, let's keep in touch on QQ!"

On the way back, the 39 Sichuan-Shu contestants were on three separate trains.

Because there were only three direct trains a day between the two cities!

In a few days it would be the New Year, which was the peak of the Spring Festival travel rush for migrant workers returning home. The staff from *Sprout* had to help them book the tickets; it was extremely difficult to buy them on your own.

Chen Guiliang hadn't taken a plane when he came, so he certainly wouldn't on the way back.

If he were to fly off alone, other contestants would inevitably post threads to slander him. God knows how many people were red-eyed with jealousy.

Upon reaching their destination, a few local students from Rongcheng left.

Six people remained on their train: three from Dafu City, two from Longdu City, and one from Tiancheng City.

"We're going to buy tickets too."

"There are probably no tickets left for today, right? The station hall is packed."

"We'll buy tickets for tomorrow and just find a hotel for the night."

"Well, you guys be safe. Goodbye."

The three from Dafu City left as well, leaving only Chen Guiliang, Mi Lan, and Zeng Jing.

Zeng Jing was a boy from Tiancheng who had won a second prize this time. His home was next to Longdu City.

"Go buy train tickets for tomorrow?" Zeng Jing asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Let's just take a bus. Train tickets are hard to get, and the hall is full of returning migrant workers. I reckon tomorrow morning's train tickets are definitely sold out, and it's hard to say if we can even get afternoon tickets."

"Alright, bus it is."

The three of them dragged their suitcases out of the train station. As soon as they exited the hall, they were swarmed by illegal taxi operators.

"Going to Zizhou? Just need the three of you."

"Emei, Emei, leaving as soon as you get on."

"Yazhou, Yazhou. No tickets at the long-distance bus station..."

Chen Guiliang found one going to Longdu and asked, "How much?"

"One hundred per person," the other party replied.

"What kind of car is it?"

"A Jinbei."

"How many more people do you need?"

"Four or five."

"Four hundred for you, leave right now."

"Deal!"

During the Spring Festival travel rush, getting ripped off was a given. Normally, the fare would be fifty or sixty yuan at most.

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to haggle. He just considered it the cost of staying in Rongcheng for the night.

He could have bargained, probably down to seventy or eighty. But the driver would definitely keep waiting for more people, and they could cram ten people into a single van (along with a small mountain of luggage).

The group continued walking, encountering various touts along the way.

Chen Guiliang ignored all those asking if they needed accommodation.

Until a middle-aged woman with a thick local accent said, "Save the people?"

Chen Guiliang couldn't help but laugh, replying, "NO."

Mi Lan didn't understand and caught up to him after a few steps, asking, "What did she just say?"

Chen Guiliang said, "She wants us to join her in saving humanity."

Mi Lan was completely baffled.

Zeng Jing, beside them, was holding back laughter so hard he was almost internally injured.

They walked to a newsstand by the road where a migrant worker couple was waiting.

The illegal transport tout who had brought Chen Guiliang over said, "You guys wait a few minutes, I've already called the driver."

Bored with waiting, Mi Lan went to the newsstand to buy a newspaper.

She specifically looked for anything related to the New Concept Competition, but unfortunately found nothing. This was because very few Shanghai newspapers were distributed to Rongcheng.

For example, the *Shanghai Youth Daily* was only circulated locally in Shanghai and its surrounding areas.

*Southern Weekly* and *Life Week* were weeklies, and the new issues wouldn't be out until tomorrow.

As for papers like the *Global Times*, they wouldn't report on the New Concept Competition at all.

After looking through them all, Mi Lan only found the *Wen Wei Po*.

She pointed excitedly at the supplement section, "Chen Guiliang, your article!"

Zeng Jing ran over to look and also exclaimed, "Damn, if you include the commentary, it takes up almost three-quarters of the page. Bro, you're famous!"

Mi Lan bought three copies of the newspaper right away, one for each of them to keep as a memento.

By the faint light of the newsstand, Chen Guiliang carefully read Dong Hongkang's commentary. The entire piece was full of praise. It first appreciated and lauded the poetry and prose, then went on to say that Chen Guiliang was a leader among contemporary literary youth, his writing style seasoned yet possessing the sharp edge and passion of a young man.

"Beep beep!"

A Jinbei van pulled up. It wasn't in terrible condition, but there were already two people inside.

The migrant worker couple by the road was the first to scramble into the van. They didn't dare put their luggage in the trunk; instead, they went through the trouble of personally guarding it, placing their large and small bags at their feet or holding them directly.

Chen Guiliang first took out four hundred yuan to pay the fare for Mi Lan and Zeng Jing, and then went to put away the luggage.

The van went to Tiancheng first, where Zeng Jing got off and waved goodbye.

Then it went to Longdu. The road conditions were so bad that it was past three in the morning by the time they arrived.

The couple was clamoring for the driver to take them back to their village. After some argument, the driver only agreed to drop them at the station.

Chen Guiliang and Mi Lan didn't get involved. They got out and hailed a cab directly. After dropping Mi Lan off outside a residential complex, Chen Guiliang took another cab to his second uncle's place.

His second aunt, Lin Chunhong, opened the door yawning. She was pleasantly surprised to see Chen Guiliang and called inside, "Feng Tao, your nephew is back!"

Feng Tao came out with a jacket draped over his shoulders, asking gleefully, "Guiliang, can you get guaranteed admission to Tsinghua or Peking University?"

"Where did you hear that?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Feng Tao said, "Brother Gang called and told me."

"Are you choosing Tsinghua or Peking University?" Lin Chunhong quickly asked as well. She hadn't even finished high school, but that didn't stop her from knowing how incredible Tsinghua and Peking University were.

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "It's not certain yet. It's still up in the air whether Tsinghua or Peking University will even recruit me."

Lin Chunhong pressed, "Didn't they say Tsinghua and Peking University are fighting over people?"

"It's a rumor," Chen Guiliang asked, "How did Brother Gang find out?"

Feng Tao said, "Tao Xue saw it online."

Over ten hours earlier.

Tao Xue was happily playing as a female Daoist priest in a private server set up by her brother.

Her phone rang. After answering, her roommate Yu Tian said, "Quick, log in to the *Sprout* forum!"

"What's wrong? I'm in the middle of a game," Tao Xue asked.

Yu Tian said, "That older schoolmate of yours, your grand-nephew, won first prize. He's famous on the forum!"

Tao Xue quickly quit the game, browsed through the posts on the *Sprout* forum carefully, and then rushed to her brother's place next door.

"Bro, come and see!"

"I just got back late last night, can't you let me sleep a bit more?"

"Chen Guiliang is famous!"

These past few days, Tao Chenggang had been doing offline promotion in neighboring cities and counties, looking for more internet cafes to partner with in operating *Abyss Legend*.

With the Spring Festival approaching, he planned to take a break.

He was also using the internet and his phone to contact a game development team, planning to try making his own game next year.

He only had a few hundred thousand in initial startup capital. The plan was to sell two internet cafes first, while continuing to operate the private server and the other cafes. When the money started running low, he'd sell two more. It's not like there was a shortage of buyers for them.

He would continue until all the internet cafes were sold.

Tao Chenggang was dragged to the computer by his sister. After reading a few posts, he was utterly shocked and said, "Damn, that's awesome!"

"I'm going to enter the New Concept Competition too when I'm a high school senior," Tao Xue said.

Tao Chenggang poured cold water on her enthusiasm, "Can you write an article like that?"

Tao Xue said, "I'm great at writing compositions too."

"Focus on your studies, play fewer games, and read fewer extracurricular books." Tao Chenggang slapped her on the top of the head.

Tao Xue clutched her head, fuming, "Don't hit my head again, it'll make me stupid!"

"As if you're so smart," Tao Chenggang went to the fridge to look for food. "Where are Mom and Dad?"

Tao Xue said, "Dad was on the night shift last night, he's sleeping. Mom went to work."

Tao Chenggang took out half a plate of cured meat and commanded while eating, "Go cook some rice."

"I only know how to cook rice, not other dishes." Tao Xue grudgingly went to wash the rice.

After putting the rice in the electric cooker, she ran back to the computer, giggling foolishly as she looked at the posts.

Then Tao Xue logged into QQ and left messages for her classmates one by one: "My grand-nephew won first prize in the New Concept Competition, it's Chen Guiliang from the senior class. Quick, go look at the *Sprout* forum, a bunch of famous schools like Tsinghua and Peking University are fighting to get him!"

Finally, Tao Xue couldn't resist and called Bian Guanyue.

"Senior, what are you busy with?"

"Doing practice papers."

"My grand-nephew won first prize."

"Really?"

"Haha, you didn't even know. Hanging up."

Bian Guanyue stood there in a daze, holding her phone, feeling a bit sour.

She thought Chen Guiliang had called Tao Xue to share the good news but hadn't told her.

Bian Guanyue opened her laptop and searched Baidu for the keywords "Chen Guiliang" and "New Concept first prize."

A pile of search results quickly appeared.

They were mainly concentrated on major forums and the *Sprout* official website.

Bian Guanyue muttered to herself, "That little rascal tricked me again, she saw it online too."

Bian Guanyue browsed through the posts over and over again when her phone suddenly rang loudly.

"Hello, may I speak with Ms. Bian Guanyue?" A strange man's voice came from the other end.

Bian Guanyue replied, "This is she. What can I do for you?"

The man said, "I am Chen Sihe, the director of the Chinese Department at Fudan University."

Bian Guanyue was baffled and replied subconsciously, "Hello, Director Chen."

"Student Chen Guiliang left this number as an emergency contact," Chen Sihe chuckled. "You must be Chen Guiliang's mother, right?"

"Huh?" Bian Guanyue was a bit stunned.

Chen Sihe said, "Here's the situation. Fudan has always valued the cultivation of outstanding literary talent, and we are very optimistic about your son. We held an emergency meeting yesterday and managed to secure some more favorable conditions..."

"No," Bian Guanyue quickly explained, "I'm Chen Guiliang's classmate. Not his mom!"

"..." The other end of the line fell silent.

Bian Guanyue asked, "Director Chen, are you still there?"

Chen Sihe clearly sighed, "Hello, Student Bian Guanyue. Could you please try to persuade Chen Guiliang? We at Fudan are very sincere. Please trouble yourself to inform him that the original admission offer based on the bachelor's degree threshold remains unchanged; with his usual grades, that's certainly not a problem. In addition, he can choose any major in the liberal arts, and if he wants to pursue graduate studies, we can guarantee him a spot. There's also the student union and party membership..."

"Wait a moment, let me get something to write this down." Bian Guanyue was afraid of missing something.

After the call ended, Bian Guanyue jumped up, celebrating silently with flailing arms and legs.

She was happy for Chen Guiliang, but even happier that he had listed her as his emergency contact.

Bian Guanyue stopped doing her practice papers and paced back and forth in her bedroom.

Remembering that her grandparents had gone out to play cards and weren't home, she stepped into the living room with the gait of a Sichuan opera performer, raised a hand as if gently fanning herself with a folding fan, and sang a cheerful excerpt from the Sichuan opera *The Legend of the White Snake*: "The spring light is fine, a hundred flowers bloom, on Su Causeway the willows line row on row. The sound of flutes and drums from painted boats is crisp, a flower-selling girl crosses the stone steps. This mortal world is better than the fairy realm of Penglai, who would wish to return to Mount Emei for bitter cultivation?"

"Meow meow~~~"

The calico cat she had bought a few days ago had grown accustomed to her by now. It came out from under the sofa and pounced around her feet.

"You're happy too?"

Bian Guanyue scooped up the little cat, rolled onto the sofa to lie down, and played with its pink little paws.

"Meow~"

"Aww! I'm gonna bite you."

"Meow~"

"Come, I'll teach you to dance."

Footsteps sounded from outside the door, followed by the sound of a key being inserted into the lock.

Bian Guanyue immediately put the kitten down and walked back to her bedroom nonchalantly, "Grandpa, the rice is cooking in the rice cooker. You just need to cook the dishes."

Here in Sichuan-Shu, there wasn't much of a stir in the newspapers and magazines; only the supplement of *Wen Wei Po* attracted a small amount of attention.

But it was a different story in the Yangtze River Delta region.

So many newspapers were making a collective effort. At the very least, they would give it a small blurb, and some newspapers even dedicated half a page to a detailed report.

Some newspapers also compared Chen Guiliang with Han Han and Guo Xiaosi, saying that Han Han was racing cars and Guo Xiaosi was plagiarizing. Both of them were already cases of 'lamenting Zhong Yong.' How could they ensure that Chen Guiliang would not repeat their mistakes?

Some took the opportunity to discuss education, debating whether such specialists should be specially recruited, and if so, how they should be cultivated.

"Composing a poem in seven steps," "universities fighting over a talent," "Chen Guiliang angrily confronts Guo Xiaosi over plagiarism"... this mix of true and false content was incredibly eye-catching to readers and quickly sparked heated discussion in the Yangtze River Delta region.

It wasn't until *Southern Weekly* was published that it finally triggered a nationwide discussion.

*Southern Weekly*'s headline was: *Entering a Prestigious University in Seven Steps, How to Balance Specially Recruited Geniuses and Educational Fairness?*

The *Southern Weekly* reporter was skilled at stirring up trouble, listing past winners from the first and second competitions who had been given guaranteed admission, many of whom had since faded into obscurity. They added fuel to the fire by describing how universities were vying for Chen Guiliang. Then they touched upon the hot topic of educational fairness that had been debated over the past two years.

It also mentioned that with his usual grades, Chen Guiliang could at best get into a second-tier university. Was it really reasonable for Tsinghua, Peking University, and Fudan to recruit him?

After this report came out, the major newspapers indeed began to engage in a war of words!

The media in Sichuan-Shu were slow to react. A literary talent had emerged from their own province, and they only found out about it through newspapers from other provinces. They could only rush to reprint related news or repost threads from forums.

The *West China Metropolis Daily* was the best-selling newspaper in all of Sichuan. On the 28th day of the twelfth lunar month, with just two days left before New Year's Eve, reporter Chen Feng (pen name) couldn't wait and set off, driving straight for Longdu.

He didn't have Chen Guiliang's contact information, so he could only go to Fushi County No. 2 Middle School to find the school leaders and teachers first.
